geo.label: hold / data dependent
parts: Macro Stance

Growth is slowing without breaking, and the Fed has no reason to move while the data stay mixed. Reuters reported that parts of the Treasury market are already worried about a pause in rate cuts [[n10321]]. February’s ISM services reading came in at 53.5 [[n9958]] and manufacturing at 50.3 [[n9735]], so activity is positive but thin. Private payrolls slowed: ADP showed US firms added 77,000 jobs, the smallest gain since July [[n9976]]. Weekly jobless claims jumped to 242,000 [[n9625]]. The Atlanta Fed model pointed to first-quarter growth of negative 1.5 percent [[n10095]], and WSJ framed the risk as stagflation [[n10346]].
Rates & Curve

The two-year yield is 3.99% and the 10-year is 4.28% at the prior close, with the 30-year at 4.57% (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-05). The 10-year minus two-year spread is +29 bps, positively sloped and not steep. Over 20 observations the two-year fell 22 bps and the 10-year fell 24 bps, so the spread narrowed 2 bps: a bull flattening, with both yields lower and the 10-year lower by more. Over five observations the two-year is down 6 bps while the 10-year rose 3 bps, which says the rally has paused rather than reversed (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-05). Equities show the strain. The S&P 500 closed at 5,842.63, up 1.12% in the prior session but down 3.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The VIX closed at 21.93 after a 27.43% rise over 20 sessions, and the dollar index stands at 105.74 index points, down 2.06% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
New / Most Important

The tariff sequence is the new fact. Trump’s Canada and Mexico duties were set to start on Tuesday, and stocks fell on the news [[n4276]]. Then the White House exempted some automakers for one month [[n4558]]. Reuters suggested pickup trucks explained the delay [[n10424]], carmakers were given a monthlong reprieve [[n10387]], and the New York Times noted that other levies continue [[n2969]]. The S&P 500 rose 1.12% in the prior session on that relief (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Relief is not removal: Automotive News warned that tariffs could wipe out Detroit 3 profits [[n8637]].
Playbook ✓

Hold the curve trade. The long end is rallying harder than the front, so stay long duration in the belly and avoid adding steepeners. Hold equities at market weight and buy protection through the tariff window while the VIX sits near 22, because a one-day rally does not remove the policy risk. Trim the consumer-discretionary names that have not shown they can pass tariffs on to customers. Change the call if the two-year yield climbs back above its 20-session reference of 4.21%, because that would mean the market is pricing the pause out of the curve (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-05).

geo.label: fiscal pivot in Germany
parts: Macro Stance

Europe’s policy direction has changed. The ECB faces tougher calls ahead [[n3238]], but the bigger shift is fiscal. Germany’s parties agreed a historic overhaul of the debt brake to revamp the military and the economy [[n3328]]. Fortune put the package at $1.3 trillion [[n3300]], and the European Commission unveiled a €800bn plan to rearm Europe [[n3256]]. Markets are reading it as a regime change rather than a one-off.
Credit & Inflation

Credit is calmer than the currency suggests. Italy’s spread over Germany has dropped below 100 basis points [[n3324]], so the periphery risk premium that dominated the last crisis is now a footnote. Euro-area unemployment is 6.2 percent [[n9814]], with Italy improving but still among the highest. Inflation eased slightly in February [[n3262]], which gives the ECB room to stay patient. The DAX closed at 23,081.03, up 6.93% over 20 sessions, and the Euro Stoxx 50 at 5,489.12, up 4.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). EUR/USD is at 1.0627, up 2.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
New / Most Important

The DAX cleared 23,000 for the first time [[n3219]], and Reuters reported that stocks and the euro cheered the debt-brake deal while bonds fell [[n3259]]. The execution risk is real: Merz is still racing to win support for the package [[n3332]], and Bloomberg wrote that Germany is loosening its fiscal chains to transform European defence [[n3330]]. The cleanest expression is in defence and the industrials that supply it, and European defence shares have hit record highs [[n3204]].
Playbook ✓

Stay overweight European cyclicals and domestic-facing banks against the US multiple, and keep a defence-supplier position sized to the spending rather than to the news flow. Add on pullbacks that hold the DAX above its 20-session reference of 21,585.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-05). What would change the call is a failed parliamentary vote on the package, which would take the German leadership out of the trade.

geo.label: targets set, demand still soft
parts: Macro Stance

Beijing’s 2025 framework is expansionary on paper. The government set growth at around 5% [[n1405]] and an inflation goal of around 2% [[n1263]], and it set the deficit at around 4% of GDP, a record [[n1407]]. Bloomberg put the official budget deficit at its highest in more than 30 years [[n1390]]. Reuters described the stimulus as a response to changes unseen in a century [[n1242]], and it reported that Beijing put consumer spending ahead of technology [[n1241]]. The message is that Beijing will spend to protect growth against tariffs rather than wait for them to fade.
PMIs & Activity

The surveys show a rebound from a soft base. Reuters reported that factory activity picked up in February, though trade uncertainty weighed on the outlook [[n1080]]. The non-manufacturing index was 50.4 in February [[n1049]], which keeps services barely in expansion. January’s private factory survey had shown growth slowing [[n0455]], so the February pickup is a recovery from a low rather than a new cycle. Prices are still soft: consumer inflation was 0.5% in January [[n0591]], and producer deflation persisted [[n0592]]. In Hong Kong, retail sales value fell 3.2% in January [[n1150]], a reminder that the consumer is still soft even as stocks rally.
Credit Impulse

Credit turned up at the start of the year. Reuters reported that China’s January bank lending hit a record high on policy stimulus [[n0707]], and that the property loan contraction eased after government support [[n0694]]. The fiscal window widened as Beijing stepped up spending to counter the tariffs [[n1417]]. The impulse is front-loaded, so the test is whether lending holds its pace once the January surge fades.
Property

Property is still the drag. A Reuters poll sees home prices falling further, with no recovery until 2026 [[n0823]]. Second-hand home prices narrowed their decline for a seventh straight month in February, a report said [[n1078]]. The Financial Times wrote that the state is propping up the housing market [[n0828]], and Reuters reported that hedge funds are betting on a turnaround in the unloved sector [[n0895]]. The Economist framed the policy moment as a test of Xi Jinping on deflation [[n1093]]. Improvement in the monthly data is still only a narrowing of the decline. Hong Kong’s banks face rising risks amid the prolonged property slump, Moody’s warned [[n0779]].
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

Trade is the policy story. China hit back at US farm goods with extra tariffs of 10% to 15% [[n1126]], and its extra duties of up to 15% on some US goods start on March 10 [[n1125]]. It added 15 US companies to its export control list [[n1233]] and banned imports of Illumina’s gene sequencers [[n1237]]. Beijing is still signalling a willingness to talk while it retaliates [[n1243]]. Defence spending rises 7.2% in 2025 [[n1250]], and Beijing plans to boost food imports from Latin America and Europe as the trade war escalates [[n1414]]. Fiscal support is the offset.
Markets & Flows

Equities carry the rally. The Hang Seng closed at 23,594.21, up 2.84% in the prior session and 14.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The Shanghai Composite closed at 3,341.97 index points, up 3.48% over 20 sessions. The China A-share ETF ASHR closed at 27.02 USD, and KWEB, the China internet ETF, closed at 36.68 USD, up 14.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). USD/CNY closed at 7.2651, up 1.16% over 20 sessions, so the currency is steady (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). S&P Global wrote that Chinese equities are on track for a major boost from an insurance investment directive [[n1398]], and TradingView reported Asian markets rallying as Alibaba jumped on its AI push [[n1382]]. Hong Kong’s listing market is running hot as well: the bubble-tea chain Mixue popped 47% on debut as Hong Kong IPO volumes rebounded [[n5849]].
New / Most Important

The insurance directive is the most important signal, because it is a lever aimed at the equity market itself rather than at the growth targets [[n1398]]. Reuters reported that Trump’s cheap-yuan comment is unfounded, which removes one of the currency arguments against Chinese assets [[n1271]]. The fiscal tilt is visible in the numbers: the official budget deficit is at its highest in more than 30 years [[n1390]]. The Hang Seng’s 2.84% gain in the prior session shows the market is already acting on it (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Playbook ✓

Own the internet and platform names on dips, using KWEB as the liquid vehicle, and keep USD/CNY exposure small because the currency is steady at 7.2651. Add on a Shanghai Composite close that holds above its 20-session reference of 3,229.49 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-05). Cut if the insurance directive is not followed by inflows. ⚠ Divergence: the Hang Seng is up 14.55% over 20 sessions while the property data still show home prices falling, so equities are running ahead of the real-economy evidence (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).

geo.label: rate-hike path, weak yen trade
parts: Macro Stance

Japan is leaving easy policy, and the bond market is running ahead of the central bank. The 10-year yield hit its highest level in over 15 years [[n4961]], and CNBC put it near 16-year highs on rate-hike expectations and a global sell-off [[n4966]]. Inflation keeps the BOJ on its hike path [[n4769]]: the inflation rate climbed to a 2-year high of 4% in January [[n4758]]. The BOJ governor warned of strong global uncertainty from US tariffs [[n4808]], which is the counterweight to the hike case.
Activity & Currency

Traders have placed a record bet on a stronger yen, eyeing further rate hikes [[n4918]]. USD/JPY closed at 149.7990, down 2.81% over 20 sessions from 154.1330 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The Nikkei 225 closed at 37,418.24, down 2.86% over 20 sessions, though it rose 0.23% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Corporate spending is pulling back: Reuters reported that Japanese capex dropped for the first time in four years amid tariff fears [[n4898]], and Sony and Suntory are building US stockpiles as the tariff threat grows [[n4977]]. Yen-selling pressure persists despite Trump’s warning shot, Nikkei Asia reported [[n4982]].
Playbook ✓

Trim the Nikkei into strength and hedge yen exposure for dollar-based holders, since a stronger yen cuts the value of overseas earnings while the front end prices hikes. Favour domestic-rate beneficiaries only on a pullback. Change the call if USD/JPY breaks back above 150, which would mean the yen trade has run out of room and the tariff drag on exporters becomes the dominant risk (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).

geo.label: growth firm, banks wobble
parts: Macro Stance

Australia’s activity data gave the RBA room to keep a hawkish tone. GDP grew 1.3% in the fourth quarter, supported by exports [[n0299]], and Bloomberg tied the print to the central bank’s hawkish tone [[n0303]]. The growth rate hit a two-year high [[n0294]], and the economy exited a 21-month per-capita recession [[n0300]]. The AFR published the chart the RBA used to justify its latest rate cut [[n0383]], which is the anchor for the next decision.
Demand & Financing

Households are the swing factor. CoreLogic data show the housing market ending its downturn as the rate cut lifted sentiment [[n0208]]. Chalmers is upbeat, but economists warn of a shallow recovery [[n0356]]. The bank trade is the nervous point: short sellers ditched CBA as sell-off doubts mounted [[n0378]], and CBA completed its exit from Vietnam’s VIB after a 4.4% stake sale [[n0347]]. The ASX 200 closed at 8,141.10, down 3.28% over 20 sessions from 8,416.90 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). AUD/USD closed at 0.6270, up 0.30% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), and Fortescue, the iron ore miner, closed at 15.93 AUD, down 16.11% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Playbook ✓

Own the growth beneficiaries rather than the banks until short interest in CBA falls, and keep AUD exposure small against a dollar that is still drifting lower. Miners with iron ore exposure need the commodity to steady before they re-rate. What would change the call: a sharper fall in the AUD or a clear reversal in bank short interest. ⚠ Divergence: the GDP beat says growth is firm, but the ASX is down 3.28% over 20 sessions, so the equity market is discounting the bank and dividend story rather than the macro upturn (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).

geo.label: PMI turn, zloty near highs
parts: Macro Stance

Poland’s cycle is turning up, and the central bank has to watch inflation. Manufacturing shows signs of recovery for the first time in almost three years [[n5089]], and a PMI reading signalled the end of an almost three-year industrial recession [[n5532]]. GDP grew 2.9% in 2024, beating forecasts [[n4983]], and the latest quarterly reading showed acceleration, though below what was expected [[n5193]]. Inflation is still the constraint: Business Insider Polska called rising prices a strong argument for the central bank on rates [[n5204]], and January’s consumer prices edged higher [[n5202]]. Wages rose strongly in 2024, the statistics office showed [[n5229]], and the finance minister called 2025 a breakthrough year as the economy accelerates [[n5263]]. Poland and Czechia have the lowest unemployment in the European Union, according to Eurostat [[n5604]].
Markets

The zloty is the trade. Bloomberg reported the zloty at a 10-year high against the dollar, fanned by a hawkish central bank [[n5034]], and Rzeczpospolita reported it beating a seven-year record [[n5282]]. USD/PLN closed at 3.9165, down 3.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), and EUR/PLN at 4.1608, down 1.11% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Parkiet asked whether a strong zloty will carry the WIG20 to a new record [[n5659]]. The WIG20 total-return tracker closed at 49.23 PLN, up 8.07% over 20 sessions, and the US-listed Poland ETF EPOL closed at 26.92 USD, up 14.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Foreigners are in the bond market: more than ten central banks hold Polish treasuries [[n5520]], and Money.pl reported foreign central banks buying them [[n5535]]. Parkiet’s fear index is the sentiment check [[n5626]].
Fiscal & Politics

Fiscal policy is the weak point. Economist Leszek Balcerowicz criticised the Tusk government for spending that makes no sense [[n5333]], and Bankier.pl quoted him again on spending that serves no purpose [[n5382]]. The finance minister’s line is that 2025 is a breakthrough year [[n5263]], which is the government’s answer. Credit holidays are not coming back, and the government points to another solution [[n5667]]. Politics is a risk: a far-right candidate’s rise has turned the presidential race into a three-horse contest [[n5045]], and Politico wrote that Poland’s nationalists stick to Trump like glue [[n5044]].
Corporate & Sectors

Earnings separate the quality names. Orlen posted a record profit [[n5442]] and a historic dividend [[n5327]], and its Czech refineries are again without Russian oil but have a Western alternative [[n5559]]. PKN closed at 63.27 PLN, up 15.35% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Bank Pekao made 6.4 billion zloty and wants half of it for dividends [[n5314]]; PEO closed at 170.20 PLN, up 9.10% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Dino Polska hit a record high on a weak market [[n5391]] and presented its 2025 plans [[n5389]]; DNP closed at 488.20 PLN, up 6.90% over 20 sessions. At mBank, 25 thousand franc-loan borrowers have settled [[n5634]], and MBK closed at 736.00 PLN, up 20.03% over 20 sessions. Business Insider Polska reported a series of seismic shocks at two KGHM mines [[n5359]], and PGE is discussing a second nuclear plant at Bełchatów [[n5487]]. CD Projekt drew attention for its Witcher 4 character design, with the studio explaining the changes [[n5432]], but it is a product story rather than an earnings one.
Geopolitics & Security

Defence is the demand driver. Poland said it will spend 4.7% of GDP on defence this year [[n4995]], and Poland and South Korea signed a security agreement [[n5088]]. Poland sent a large batch of T-72 tanks to Ukraine [[n5067]], and it revealed what the Starlink terminals for Ukraine cost [[n5078]]. Russian operatives were reportedly paid to paint anti-government graffiti in Poland [[n5035]], and the Polish space agency is investigating a cyberattack on its systems [[n5062]]. Defence producers are the market’s clearest winners in Warsaw [[n5675]]. Ukrainian stocks surged on the Warsaw exchange in February on talk of a peace plan [[n5003]].
New / Most Important

The one signal that matters is the PMI turn, because it moves the story from currency carry to real growth. Manufacturing is recovering for the first time in almost three years [[n5089]], which is why the zloty and the WIG20 can rise together. Santander Bank warned that a strong zloty may weigh on GDP [[n5358]]: the same currency strength that draws foreign money also cuts into the export earnings that carry the recovery.
Playbook ✓

Buy the banks and the defence names on pullbacks, keep zloty exposure, and hedge only on a 20-session move against you. Change the call if the next inflation print surprises higher, because that would push back the date at which rates can fall. ⚠ Divergence: the zloty and the WIG20 are rising on growth hopes while the fiscal criticism is getting louder [[n5333]], so the market is pricing the growth recovery but not the budget.
Narrative

Technology is carrying the consensus and losing the tape. The technology sector ETF closed at 221.57 USD, up 1.41% in the prior session but down 4.07% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The AI case is intact at the software layer: Microsoft’s $13 billion OpenAI investment cleared a UK review [[n8491]], and Apple’s App Store revenue rose 14% as ChatGPT drove growth [[n2902]].
Reported

Apple cut the price of its MacBook Air by $100 despite tariffs [[n8291]], and Intel defeated a shareholder lawsuit over foundry losses that the headline puts at $32 billion [[n8445]]. Dell’s full-year 2025 earnings per share beat expectations [[n0396]].
EPS Upside Watch

Dell is set up for upside on capital returns. It raised its dividend 18% and launched a $10 billion buyback [[n3567]] after its earnings beat, and the buyback is the part of the story the market can count.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The consensus says AI demand cannot be stopped. The counter-signal is that Nvidia’s optimistic forecast failed to convince Wall Street [[n0390]], and that a Summit Insights downgrade cited AI market concerns [[n2743]]. Nvidia shares fell 9% on tariff fears [[n2745]].
Narrative

Communication services has lost momentum even though the AI advertising story is intact. The sector ETF closed at 101.47 USD, down 1.98% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), and Alphabet is the drag, down 16.16% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Google announced layoffs in its HR and cloud units as part of ongoing cost cuts [[n9586]], and an advertising outage cost tens of thousands in ad revenue over a weekend [[n2875]].
Reported
Warner Bros. Discovery added 6.4 million Max subscribers and forecast 150 million by the end of 2026 [[n2573]]. That is the growth case in the sector.
EPS Upside Watch

Disney is set up for margin upside rather than revenue upside. It cut 6% of its ABC network and entertainment TV workforce [[n8362]] and shut the data-driven website 538 [[n8367]]. That cost discipline shows up first in margins.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The AI-winner reading meets cost cuts. An upgrade said Alphabet’s future looks brighter than the Big Tech alternatives, pointing to Waymo and Willow [[n7662]], while the same company is cutting staff in its cloud and HR units [[n9586]]. The consensus cannot hold both, so the stock is being read as an option on AI rather than as a cost story.
Narrative

Banks have the cleanest earnings story and the most fragile credit story. The financial sector ETF closed at 50.21 USD, up 0.58% in the prior session and down 1.82% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). JPMorgan closed at 251.53 USD, down 6.12% over 20 sessions, and Goldman Sachs at 593.07 USD, down 6.48%, while the regional bank ETF KRE is down 8.34% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Reported

Goldman Sachs’ full-year 2024 results beat expectations [[n2720]], and BNY Mellon’s revenue beat while earnings per share were in line [[n2691]]. Customers Bancorp missed on EPS [[n2912]], and Ready Capital’s shares plunged 28% after a fourth-quarter loss and a dividend cut [[n2753]].
EPS Upside Watch

Investment banks and asset managers are set up for upside if deal flow holds. Blackstone beat its full-year expectations [[n2908]], and Millennium committed $1 billion to a stock picker [[n3703]]. Banks are regaining ground in lending as private credit eases off mega loan deals [[n1466]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

The consumer-credit story is the counter-signal. Fitch says credit card performance is deteriorating [[n1439]], and credit spreads are on their longest widening streak since 2023 [[n3564]]. Earnings can beat while the loan book weakens.
Narrative

Energy has lost its geopolitical premium as supply keeps coming. WTI closed at 66.31 USD, down 8.79% over 20 sessions, and Brent at 69.30 USD, down 9.06% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The energy ETF closed at 85.70 USD, down 4.82% over 20 sessions. OPEC+ agreed to gradually hike output from April [[n7969]], and February output rose as Iran’s exports kept flowing [[n8545]].
Reported

Saudi Aramco posted a drop in full-year profit and slashed its dividend [[n2863]], and it expects a lower 2025 dividend after net income fell [[n2806]]. Colombia’s Ecopetrol saw profit slide 22% in 2024 [[n2856]].
EPS Upside Watch

Natural gas is the only energy line with upside in the price data. Henry Hub natural gas closed at 4.45 USD per MMBtu, up 36.80% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Oil names have no upside surprise on current prices.
⚡ Breaking Convention
The geopolitical premium that supports oil is failing to hold, and one commentary argued that Trump has exposed OPEC’s diminished market power [[n8325]].
Narrative

Defence and aerospace lead the sector’s story, and Europe’s rearmament is the engine. The industrial sector ETF closed at 133.85 USD, down 2.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Europe announced an $840 billion rearmament plan that sent BAE and Thales soaring [[n7780]], and Citi said Lockheed and five other defence stocks look like buys after a slump [[n8467]].
Reported
Thales’ shares soared after its 2024 results beat forecasts on defence spending [[n2877]]. Bunzl’s shares fell on lower pretax profit [[n2696]].
EPS Upside Watch

Boeing is set up for upside only on execution. Its CEO told staff the company must change its insular culture [[n8317]], and a joint venture was selected to build the South Carolina site expansion [[n7697]]. Boeing closed at 163.16 USD, down 7.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
⚡ Breaking Convention

Defence demand is not the constraint in this sector; execution is. Emirates said it will spend $5 billion refitting its aircraft [[n8382]], and Boeing’s culture problem [[n8317]] is the reason to doubt that aircraft supply can keep up with demand.
Narrative

The consumer sector is absorbing the tariff shock, and the names with pricing power are telling the story. The consumer discretionary ETF closed at 211.41 USD, down 8.80% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Best Buy warned that price increases from tariffs were “highly likely” [[n2810]], and Abercrombie & Fitch predicted a tariff hit [[n6061]].
Reported

Target’s sales fell but its earnings topped expectations [[n0421]]. Adidas’ fourth-quarter sales topped expectations as its final Yeezy stock sold off [[n2896]], and Foot Locker’s results show the sneaker industry, and Nike, still have more pain ahead [[n2921]].
EPS Upside Watch

Target is set up for a surprise only if its growth plan works. It unveiled a $15 billion sales growth strategy [[n3800]] while bracing for first-quarter profit pressure from tariffs and low demand [[n2873]].
⚡ Breaking Convention

Tesla is the consumer-discretionary story in one stock. Its China-made EV sales fell to their lowest since August 2022 [[n8062]], and the shares are down 28.84% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The sector reads as weak across the board, but brand-led names are being judged on their own stories.
Narrative

Staples are the defensive trade, and the defence is working for some names. The staples ETF closed at 82.44 USD, up 4.86% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Coca-Cola closed at 70.08 USD, up 11.82% over 20 sessions, and PepsiCo at 153.88 USD, up 7.24% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Reported
Unilever and Procter & Gamble profits came under pressure as shoppers turned to smaller food brands [[n2761]]. Target’s chief said Mexico’s tariffs could raise produce prices within days [[n2883]].
EPS Upside Watch

Walmart and Costco are set up on trade-down. Shoppers moving to cheaper formats favour the value channel [[n2761]], and Costco closed at 1,047.75 USD, up 2.53% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The upside sits with the stores that absorb the shift, not with the brands losing share.
⚡ Breaking Convention
Japanese consumers are hunting for bargains as food inflation bites [[n2729]], which cuts against the pricing-power story that supports staples multiples.
Narrative

Obesity drugs are the sector’s growth story and its price problem. Eli Lilly closed at 929.72 USD, up 12.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Novo Nordisk is selling Wegovy for $499 a month to cash-paying US customers [[n8532]], after cutting its prices in a move that followed Eli Lilly’s [[n8524]]. Amgen started two late-stage trials for its MariTide obesity drug [[n8265]].
Reported
UnitedHealth’s full-year 2024 earnings missed expectations [[n0410]], and AstraZeneca’s shares rose 3% after a regulatory approval that expands the use of its cancer drug Imfinzi [[n7019]].
EPS Upside Watch
Eli Lilly is set up for upside on estimate revisions. Wells Fargo kept its Buy rating and raised its target to $1,100 [[n8715]]. The price cut is the risk to watch, not a reason to be short.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The consensus treats pricing power as safe, and Novo’s cash price cut says otherwise [[n8532]]. Lilly’s gain comes while its rival is cutting price [[n8524]], so the sector’s margin story now depends on volume.
Narrative

Materials are a tariff trade, not a growth trade. Copper closed at 4.77 USD, up 9.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Bloomberg reported that US copper prices surged as Trump signalled a 25% tariff on imports [[n8677]]. Copper is an asset priced for the grid and data-centre build, and this rally is about the tariff and the supply, not about China’s growth.
Reported
Fortescue, the iron ore miner, is down 16.11% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), and iron ore volatility sparked global concern, OilPrice.com reported [[n0313]].
EPS Upside Watch

Gold miners are set up for upside if the dollar keeps losing ground. The dollar index is down 2.06% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), and a Reuters poll sees the dollar losing its lustre on trade war jitters [[n3812]]. Newmont closed at 43.85 USD, up 1.15% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The copper-as-growth-gauge reading does not fit this tape. The metal is rising on tariffs and supply, while China’s non-manufacturing index at 50.4 [[n1049]] is barely expanding. That makes copper an asset to own for its own reasons, not a signal about China.
Narrative

Real estate is getting the rate tailwind. The 10-year yield is down 24 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-05), and the 30-year mortgage rate is the lowest since October [[n9946]]. The real estate ETF closed at 43.42 USD, up 5.01% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Reported
Green Street reported a large-format retail asset sold on a 6.14% yield [[n6063]], and JLL said investment appetite for grocery-anchored retail remains robust [[n6087]].
EPS Upside Watch

Mortgage-linked names are set up for upside if rates keep easing. Homebuyers are making bigger down payments but still struggle to raise the cash [[n9831]], and a lower rate eases that constraint first.
⚡ Breaking Convention
The rate story has a cost story. Rising property insurance costs are stressing multifamily housing [[n10325]], and tariffs could raise new-home prices for buyers [[n1478]].
Narrative

The AI power trade is fading. Constellation closed at 229.32 USD, down 25.14% over 20 sessions, and Vistra at 126.87 USD, down 24.63% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). CNBC wrote that the power stock at the centre of the AI trade is fading as impatient investors await a data-centre deal [[n5839]]. The utilities ETF closed at 77.49 USD, down 0.15% over 20 sessions.
Reported
Sempra’s shares slumped after a dour 2025 profit forecast on high costs [[n2329]]. Edison International said the cause of the Eaton fire could take 12 to 18 months to determine [[n2705]].
EPS Upside Watch

Contracted renewables are the safer upside. Demand for renewable energy projects remains strong, but supply is growing [[n2915]], so contract wins matter more than power prices. US small modular reactor deals remain elusive for NuScale [[n2970]], which keeps that upside on the watch list.
⚡ Breaking Convention

Retail sentiment on Vistra turned bearish on the “mega growth” case after DeepSeek [[n5764]], which cuts against the AI-power consensus. The consensus expects data-centre demand to lift every power name, while the market is discounting the ones without a signed deal.
Narrative

European autos are absorbing three policy changes at once: US tariffs, the emissions debate and a push toward cheaper EVs. The iShares STOXX Europe 600 Automobiles & Parts ETF closed at 52.16 EUR, down 6.02% over five sessions and up 1.14% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Reuters reported that European auto stocks sank as US tariffs on Mexico and Canada kicked in [[n3261]].
Reported
Continental’s shares plunged on a revenue fall and soft guidance [[n2818]]. Mercedes is cutting headcount and lowering pay increases in its cost-cutting drive [[n2844]].
EPS Upside Watch

Volkswagen’s budget EV is the upside story. VW unveiled an entry-level EV aimed at squeezed European consumers [[n8689]], with a production version set to launch at around 20,000 euros [[n8708]]. Volkswagen closed at 105.55 EUR, up 13.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
⚡ Breaking Convention

The emissions rule is contested. One report says the Commission will water down auto emission targets [[n7728]], while another says the EU sticks to its zero-emission path for new cars [[n8378]]. The two readings do not settle the direction, so the sector’s multiple depends on which one the market believes.
Narrative

Semiconductors are caught between the AI cycle and the tariff map. The semiconductor ETF closed at 206.63 USD, down 5.19% over five sessions and 4.51% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). TSMC’s $100 billion US commitment is real, but it will not include the most advanced chips, Taiwan confirmed [[n4422]], and Qualcomm’s CEO welcomed the investment [[n7617]].
Reported
ASML’s annual report says export curbs hit customer spending in 2024 [[n8246]]. Nvidia and Broadcom are testing chips on Intel’s manufacturing process, sources said [[n2744]].
EPS Upside Watch

Nvidia’s China business is the upside watch, if the indirect channel holds. Tom’s Hardware reported that Chinese firms get Blackwell chips by ordering through nearby countries, defying US bans [[n1139]]. That is volume a tighter export rule would remove.
⚡ Breaking Convention

A Chinese scientist urged China to build an alternative to Nvidia’s CUDA software [[n8638]], which cuts against the software moat that supports the chip multiple. Investors cannot treat that moat as safe while an alternative is being pushed.

earnings_pattern.title: What the market pays for: forward numbers and cash return, not the beat
parts: Rewarded

Forward numbers and cash returns were rewarded. Rolls-Royce upgraded its forecasts and its shares soared over 18% [[n5745]]. Synopsys raised its revenue forecast on the AI chip boom, and the shares rose [[n2459]]. Snowflake posted a big earnings beat and the stock jumped [[n2445]]. Thales soared as its 2024 earnings beat forecasts on defence spending [[n2877]]. Dell lifted its dividend 18% and launched a $10 billion buyback [[n3567]] after its full-year EPS beat [[n0396]].
Punished

Beats with soft forward numbers were punished. Nvidia’s sales grew 78% with strong guidance [[n2423]], yet Reuters reported its optimistic forecast did not convince Wall Street [[n0390]], and the stock sank over 8% as earnings were no match for sky-high expectations [[n6326]]. Salesforce missed on revenue and issued disappointing guidance [[n2440]]. Norwegian Cruise Line’s shares fell despite an earnings beat [[n2622]]. Abercrombie & Fitch’s shares dropped on a tepid forecast [[n9906]], and its tariff hit was flagged in the same week [[n6061]].
Pattern

The pattern is that the market pays for the next quarter, not the last one. Trailing beats were ignored when the forward number was soft, and the rewards went to companies that raised forward numbers or returned cash. The sharpest disappointment came where the beat was already in the price. Nvidia dropped in the session after its optimistic report [[n0392]].
Attention into EPS

Attention is moving to the next print. Stocktwits flagged Vistra’s retail sentiment as bearish before its results, in the “mega growth” debate after DeepSeek [[n5764]]. Nvidia was downgraded by Summit Insights over AI market concerns [[n2743]]. The template for the next cycle is consumer guidance on tariffs: Best Buy’s warning that price increases were “highly likely” [[n2810]] is what investors will check first.
Playbook

Own the names that raise forward numbers or return cash, and sell the beats that come with soft guidance. Hedge the AI leaders into the next print, because a priced-in beat can cost 8% in a day, as Nvidia’s drop showed [[n6326]]. Trade the consumer names on tariff guidance rather than on the revenue line.

underowned.title: Uranium and small reactors / URA, CCJ, OKLO
parts: Attention Gap

Reactor and uranium names have fallen while the coverage chases the AI trade that needs them. Oklo closed at 30.29 USD, down 35.40% over 20 sessions, NuScale at 17.32 USD, down 24.63%, and Cameco at 42.99 USD, down 14.57% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The news is about deals, not demand: Oklo closed its acquisition of a radioisotope producer [[n6106]], and Siemens Energy will supply Rolls-Royce with equipment for small reactors [[n5806]].
Exposure & Risk

The instruments are the uranium ETF URA, closed at 24.67 USD and down 14.67% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), and the single names OKLO and SMR. The risk is a deal drought: US small modular reactor deals remain elusive for NuScale [[n2970]], and the high-beta names move on news alone.
Trigger to Watch

A signed hyperscaler power contract, the event CNBC says the market is waiting for [[n5839]]. Italy’s plan to return to nuclear power [[n5787]] is a policy tailwind that will not move the stocks on its own.

underowned.title: Regional banks and card lenders / KRE
parts: Attention Gap

Regional banks are quiet compared with private credit, which the coverage treats as the growth story. The regional bank ETF closed at 58.71 USD, down 8.34% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). AFR asked how to access the private credit boom [[n8431]], while Fitch’s warning on card performance [[n1439]] is the counter-signal for the lenders.
Exposure & Risk

The instrument is the regional bank ETF KRE, down 4.02% over five sessions and 8.34% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The risk is a credit-cycle bet: Ready Capital’s shares plunged 28% after a fourth-quarter loss and a dividend cut [[n2753]], and cuts like that spread when the loan book weakens.
Trigger to Watch
A second regional lender missing on EPS after Customers Bancorp did [[n2912]]. If the misses cluster, the theme becomes consensus within one reporting season.

underowned.title: Japan’s capital recycling / 9984.T, 7203.T, EWJ
parts: Attention Gap

Japanese corporate restructuring is covered as a deal story, not as a capital-return story. Seven & i said it is selling its supermarket operations and announcing a massive buyback [[n6076]], and KKR and Walmart agreed to sell the Seiyu supermarket chain for $2.5 billion [[n4968]]. Toyota closed at 2,849.50 JPY, up 4.57% over five sessions, and Sony at 3,583.00 JPY, up 6.01% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Exposure & Risk

The instruments are single names in Tokyo and the Japan ETF EWJ, which closed at 70.15 USD, up 2.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The risk is the currency: a stronger yen cuts the dollar value of yen buybacks for foreign holders, and USD/JPY sits at 149.7990 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Trigger to Watch
The 10-year yield, which has reached its highest level in over 15 years [[n4961]]. A further rise would re-rate the financials and test the buyback case in yen.

underowned.title: Emerging-market hard-currency debt / EMB
parts: Attention Gap

Emerging-market bonds get little airtime while the coverage is about tariffs. Morningstar asked whether emerging-market stocks could outperform US stocks [[n1438]], and The DESK reported that inflows to emerging-market debt beta funds could change trading patterns [[n3775]]. The dollar emerging-market bond ETF EMB closed at 91.28 USD, up 0.78% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Exposure & Risk

The instrument is EMB. The risk is a dollar rebound: the dollar index is at 105.74 index points and fell 2.06% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), so a reversal would hit the bonds.
Trigger to Watch
A further break below 105 in the dollar index, which CoinDesk reported had already happened as bitcoin surged [[n10389]]. A dollar that stays under that level keeps the carry trade intact.

crypto.title: Bitcoin is a policy trade again, and the dip-buyers are being whipsawed
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 90,623.56 USD, up 3.90% in the latest session and 7.41% over five sessions, but down 6.21% over 20 sessions from 96,623.87 on February 13 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-05). Ether closed at 2,241.98 USD, down 16.22% over 20 sessions; Solana at 146.27 USD, down 24.78%; and XRP at 2.50 USD, up 16.54% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-05). The bitcoin ETF IBIT closed at 51.44 USD, down 8.36% over 20 sessions, and Coinbase at 222.45 USD, down 20.66% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Strategy closed at 308.55 USD, up 17.20% over five sessions and down 11.42% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Bitcoin plunged $10,000 in a day as crypto leaders criticised the plan [[n1798]], then popped 6% on a hint that the reserve strategy was near [[n1909]].
New / Most Important

The reserve is still a promise without a date. The White House hosts its first crypto summit on Friday [[n6130]], and a trader eyeing a retest of $78K said the US is seen delaying the reserve [[n1910]]. Open interest in bitcoin hit its lowest level since August [[n1956]], so leverage is light and a clear reserve size would move the market quickly. Flows are the risk: the crypto market saw a record $2.9 billion of outflows [[n1737]], and spot bitcoin ETFs once bled more than $1 billion in one day [[n1548]] before an eight-day outflow streak ended [[n1637]]. El Salvador says it will keep buying bitcoin despite IMF pressure [[n1934]].
Playbook

Hold bitcoin in spot-type vehicles, size for a retest of $78K, and add only when ETF inflows return and open interest rebuilds. Treat Strategy as a levered proxy: its 20-session decline of 11.42% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05) is what leverage looks like on the way down. Trim into the reserve pops. The 96,623.87 February reference is the line: above it the reserve premium is back, below it the trade is a fade.

flows.title: Liquidity is abundant, the dollar is the swing, and buybacks are the bid
parts: Global Liquidity

Liquidity is still abundant even as policy tightens at the margin. The New York Fed’s Perli said market liquidity levels remain abundant [[n3785]]. India’s central bank announced an infusion of over $21 billion to support growth [[n3773]] and signalled it wants a banking-system liquidity surplus [[n3774]]. The Boston Fed’s work on dealer risk constraints shows that relaxing them can make the Treasury market more liquid [[n3677]], which matters because a crowded trade depends on that plumbing. The euro area is on the same plumbing, with the ECB publishing its January bank rate statistics [[n1443]].
Rates & Dollar

The dollar is the swing factor. The dollar index is at 105.74 index points, down 2.06% over 20 sessions and down 0.64% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). CoinDesk reported the index declining below 105 as bitcoin surged past $88,000 [[n10389]], and a Reuters poll says the dollar will lose its lustre on trade war jitters [[n3812]]. Long bonds are the other side of the trade: TLT closed at 90.70 USD, up 2.57% over 20 sessions, and IEF at 94.56 USD, up 1.66% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). On the curve, the two-year is down 22 bps and the 10-year down 24 bps over 20 observations, a bull flattening (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-05). Reuters reported that parts of the Treasury market are concerned about a pause in rate cuts [[n10321]].
Credit Check

Credit is wider in the middle of the market. Bloomberg reported that credit spreads are on their longest widening streak since 2023 [[n3564]], and Fitch says credit card performance is deteriorating [[n1439]]. High yield has held: HYG closed at 79.62 USD, up 0.14% over 20 sessions and down 0.55% over five, while investment-grade LQD closed at 108.83 USD, up 1.28% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The junk market has not yet followed the widening. In Europe, Italy’s spread over Germany has dropped below 100 basis points [[n3324]], so the regional credit picture is not uniform.
Equity & Fund Flows

Buybacks are the main equity bid. Dell raised its dividend 18% and launched a $10 billion buyback [[n3567]], and Trip.com announced a US$400M buyback as its stock fell 12% [[n3637]]. AppLovin’s shares bounced back after its buyback news [[n3545]], and LSEG’s shares rose on a $633.8 million buyback [[n2519]]. Fund flows are mixed: spot bitcoin ETFs have seen record outflows [[n1548]], and inflows returned once an 8-day outflow streak ended [[n1637]]. The strategists are cautious. MarketWatch wrote that Wall Street’s biggest bear says the S&P 500 could drop to 4,200 [[n3815]], and Goldman Sachs warned the rally may falter after a 5% selloff [[n10217]]. The S&P 500 is down 3.23% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Hedge funds had a rough February as well, with the sector’s biggest names stung in the month [[n3585]].
Portfolio Implication

Keep equity at market weight, hedge tail risk, and prefer buyback-backed earnings over momentum with no cash behind it. Own duration: a bull flattening with the long end leading is money moving into the long end, and the 10-year is down 24 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-05). Keep credit beta small until spreads stop widening. The conditional is the dollar: a break below 105 would help emerging-market hard-currency debt, where EMB closed at 91.28 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). Cash is a position too: Berkshire Hathaway’s market value reached $1.07 trillion, surpassing Tesla [[n2692]], and Barron’s noted that Warren Buffett has been selling stocks [[n10405]].

anticipatory.title: The next US jobs report
parts: What Is Priced

The market is pricing a soft payroll print. ADP showed US firms added 77,000 jobs, the smallest gain since July [[n9976]], and a Reuters week-ahead piece framed rising investor angst as about to be tested by the jobs data [[n0398]]. Gold’s pause has been explained as a wait for the same report [[n9924]]. The two-year yield is down 22 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-05), so part of a weak print is already in the front end.
Conditional Expression

If the next jobs report confirms the ADP slowdown, the front end rallies and the flattening deepens, so buy duration on the weak print and avoid steepeners. If hiring holds, the two-year should retrace part of its 22 bps fall, and the dollar index at 105.74 index points would firm again (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Risk
The risk is a strong official number against weak private payrolls, which would leave the two-year at 3.99% and the S&P 500 at 5,842.63 exposed to a rate scare (US Treasury, prior close 2025-03-05).

anticipatory.title: The tariff clock
parts: What Is Priced

Trade policy now runs on dates. Carmakers got a monthlong reprieve from tariffs [[n10387]], and Trump exempted some automakers from the Canada and Mexico levies for one month [[n4558]]. China’s extra tariffs of up to 15% on some US goods start on March 10 [[n1125]], and Mexico said it would detail its retaliation on Sunday [[n4385]].
Conditional Expression

If the automaker pause is extended, the European and Japanese auto names keep their rebound and the S&P 500 keeps the 1.12% gain of the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). If it lapses, the autos are the first casualty. Watch the farm trade as well, since Reuters reported China targeting US soybeans and lumber in its response [[n1249]].
Risk

The risk is an escalation on the Mexican side that takes the one-month reprieve off the table. Automotive News said tariffs could wipe out Detroit 3 profits [[n8637]], which is the cost the reprieve only postpones.

anticipatory.title: The German package vote
parts: What Is Priced

The market has priced the direction of Germany’s fiscal turn, not the arithmetic. Reuters reported the parties agreed a historic overhaul [[n3328]], and Merz is still racing to win support for the package [[n3332]]. The DAX closed at 23,081.03, up 6.93% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Conditional Expression

If the package passes, German and European defence, infrastructure and industrial names keep the leadership, and Rheinmetall, which closed at 1,202.50 EUR and is up 60.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), keeps its bid. If support slips, the defence leaders are the most exposed. The Euro Stoxx 50, at 5,489.12, is the broad test.
Risk

The risk is that a stock up 60.59% in 20 sessions has priced the package before it is law. Bloomberg reported that East German voters complicate Merz’s plan to boost Ukraine defence [[n3157]], which is the political drag.

anticipatory.title: The US funding fight
parts: What Is Priced

Shutdown risk is back on the table. CNN reported that Democrats rejected the GOP funding strategy and stoked shutdown fears [[n10285]], and Politico wrote that Democrats are serious about a shutdown [[n10284]]. Axios reported that Republicans are hunting for Democratic votes to avoid one [[n10295]].
Conditional Expression

If Republicans find the votes, the shutdown premium fades and the safe-haven bid in gold and Treasuries comes off. If they do not, expect the bid to return, with gold at 2,926.00 USD as the cleanest hedge (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Risk

The risk is a political shock landing on a tape that is already rattled, with the VIX at 21.93 and up 27.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). A shutdown would also disrupt official data, which investors already worry about after the administration disbanded two expert panels on economic data [[n10352]].

catalysts.title: $DELL — the buyback is the thesis
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Dell raised its dividend 18% and launched a $10 billion buyback [[n3567]], after its full-year EPS beat expectations [[n0396]]. The thesis is that a company which beats and returns cash gets a bid under the shares while the orders keep coming.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Dell closed at 97.25 USD, down 15.91% over five sessions and down 4.35% over 20 sessions from 101.67 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The risk is the hardware sell-off that hit the AI complex the same week, when Nvidia fell 9% on tariff fears [[n2745]].
Trade Expression

Buy in two tranches on the five-session drawdown, and make the second tranche conditional on the next session holding the rebound. Invalidation is a further leg down that takes the shares below the five-session low, which would say the buyback is not enough.

catalysts.title: $LLY — the price cut is the test
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Wells Fargo kept its Buy rating on Eli Lilly and raised its target to $1,100 [[n8715]], while Novo Nordisk cut Wegovy prices after a similar move by Lilly [[n8524]] and offers cash-pay Wegovy at $499 a month [[n8532]]. The thesis is that Lilly’s volume gain outweighs the price cut.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Lilly closed at 929.72 USD, up 2.05% in the prior session and up 12.55% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The risk is that competition resets the pricing the multiple depends on.
Trade Expression
Own the shares on a pullback, and treat the 20-session reference of 826.07 USD as the invalidation: a close below it would undo the 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-04).

catalysts.title: $NVDA — the beat did not pay
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia’s sales grew 78% with strong guidance [[n2423]], yet Reuters reported its optimistic forecast did not convince Wall Street [[n0390]], and Summit Insights downgraded the stock over AI market concerns [[n2743]]. The short thesis is that the stock has not repriced the downgrade.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Nvidia closed at 117.30 USD, up 1.13% in the prior session but down 10.65% over five sessions and down 1.14% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The risk is a squeeze back toward the 20-session reference of 118.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-04).
Trade Expression
Use a short-dated put spread rather than a stock short, sized to the tariff news. Invalidation is a close above 118.65 USD, which would put the 20-session base back in play.

catalysts.title: $TSM — the Taiwan carve-out
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Taiwan has confirmed that TSMC’s $100 billion US investment will not include its most advanced chips [[n4422]], and Barron’s asked whether the company faces pressure to keep some chip technology in Taiwan [[n4419]]. The thesis is the split: US capacity grows while the leading edge stays at home.
Price Hurdle & Risk

TSM closed at 184.28 USD, down 5.31% over five sessions and down 9.69% over 20 sessions from 204.05 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). TSMC’s shares slid to a four-month low even as Trump reportedly planned to announce a $100 billion US chip deal [[n5955]], which says the market has partly priced the split.
Trade Expression

Own the ADR on a close above the five-session low with a stop under it, and keep the position small while the split is unresolved. Invalidation is any statement that the leading edge is moving to the US.

catalysts.title: $CRDO — the partnership news
parts: Catalyst & Thesis
Analysts highlighted Credo’s hyperscaler partnerships with Amazon, Microsoft and xAI [[n2900]]. The thesis is that these partnerships give the revenue visibility the stock has not been paid for.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Credo closed at 46.73 USD, down 13.97% in the prior session, down 23.76% over five sessions and down 38.71% over 20 sessions from 76.25 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The risk is that the partnerships are already in the price and the drawdown has more to run.
Trade Expression
A small position only, and only after a session that closes off its low. Invalidation is another session as bad as the prior one, when the stock fell 13.97%.

catalysts.title: $ORCL — the upgrade without the chase
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Wall Street’s top analysts upgraded Oracle, in a roundup of the day’s calls that also downgraded Dollar General [[n3570]]. The thesis is that the upgrade reprices the AI cloud business, which the stock has not been credited for.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Oracle closed at 161.56 USD, up 2.60% in the prior session and down 6.33% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The hurdle is the 20-session reference of 167.89 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-02-04).
Trade Expression
Buy on a close above the five-session high, with the 167.89 reference as the first target and the five-session low as the stop.

retail_intro: The dominant popular-narrative trade is buying the dip in Tesla, which echoes Tesla in 2020, GameStop in 2021 and Bitcoin in 2021, because the crowd keeps buying the founder’s story while the price is still falling.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — the inventor of our age is on sale
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The story retail tells itself is simple and personal. Tesla made electric cars matter, and Elon Musk is the founder who will turn it into a software and robotics business. Cathie Wood called him “the inventor of our age” and said he would not be distracted by DOGE [[n5984]]. Morgan Stanley said the stock could reach $430 and reinstated it as a top pick over the AI and robotics names [[n5904]], which gives the crowd a number to anchor on. The hook is the discount: the shares have lost 28.84% in 20 sessions, from 392.21 to 279.10 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), so every dip looks like a sale to people who already own the story.
What Is Driving It

The hard evidence is in the price. Tesla closed at 279.10 USD, up 2.60% in the prior session, down 4.02% over five sessions and down 28.84% over 20 sessions from 392.21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The Nasdaq 100 is down 4.35% over the same 20 sessions, so most of Tesla’s slide is stock-specific. The fundamentals explain the rest. Reuters reported that China-made EV sales fell to their lowest since August 2022 [[n8062]], and Yahoo Finance wrote that the China sales slump adds to a worrying global slowdown [[n1479]]. Reuters argued that Musk’s rallying of the far right in Europe is costing Tesla [[n2845]], and German car sales kept falling in February [[n9963]]. CNBC tied Tesla’s worst month since 2022 to Musk’s first full month in the White House [[n2876]], and Quartz called February the second-worst month ever for the stock [[n5813]].
The Social Signal

Attention is loud and two-sided. Bloomberg reported that Tesla’s 40% plunge burned Koreans who had piled into leveraged ETFs [[n5753]], which is the crowd buying the dip with borrowed exposure. A teachers’ union asked the big asset managers to check on Tesla as the stock sank “faster than a Cybertruck in quicksand” [[n5688]]. CNN described Tesla Takedown protesters gathering outside showrooms [[n6847]], and Electrek reported that Tesla’s chairwoman sold $33 million of stock [[n7472]]. Dip-buyers typically treat the protests as noise and the drawdown as a price problem rather than a franchise problem, and that is the reading the price action has to confirm.
Historical Analog

The closest mechanical analog is Tesla’s own 2020 run, which the crowd joined late. What happened first is that institutional buyers re-rated the stock on a narrative shift toward software and autonomy. What came second is that retail arrived through apps and social feeds once the move was visible, buying the story rather than the earnings path. Retail is in the second wave for the same reason now: it is buying the founder’s option on AI and robotics after the sell-side has already set a target well above the price. The difference is the direction. The 2020 wave had the price rising under it, and this one has the price falling, so today’s dip-buyers are paying for the option, not for momentum.
Smart Money View

Institutions split on pace, not on direction. Morgan Stanley’s bull case is the $430 target and the reinstatement as a top pick over the AI and robotics names [[n5904]]. The bears are in print too: a Seeking Alpha piece argued that Tesla is in a bubble the market does not want to admit [[n2773]], and Business Insider profiled a former Musk believer who expects the stock’s pain to get worse this year [[n2393]]. AP News warned that Musk’s embrace of right-wing politics risks turning off car buyers and sinking the stock [[n7295]]. The disagreement is about how fast the sales problem clears, not about whether the company is worth owning. The bulls expect a rebound once the sales data turn, and the bears expect weak deliveries to keep the shares down for longer.
When the Narrative Breaks

Watch the levels in the price data. The 20-session reference of 392.21 is the level the rebound has to reclaim before the dip can be called a bottom. The close of 279.10 is the level the crowd is defending, and a close back below the five-session low would confirm a breakdown rather than a pause. Instrument risk is the first trap: leveraged ETFs that retail uses for Tesla swings reset daily, and TQQQ closed at 72.01 USD, down 7.82% over five sessions, which shows how quickly a three-times fund resets on a drawdown (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). The dated test is expansion: Reuters reported that the US is weighing a zero tariff on cars in an India trade deal as Tesla’s entry there nears [[n4569]]. The biggest risk is a sales print that confirms the China slump [[n1479]].

retail.title: Bitcoin / BTC — the strategic reserve is coming
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Retail reads the reserve as state validation, and the story is simple. Washington has named the assets it wants to hold, bitcoin, Solana and XRP among them [[n1754]], so the floor is political. Eric Trump called the timing a win for retail investors [[n1821]], and Mexican billionaire Ricardo Salinas said he has 70% of his portfolio in bitcoin-related exposure [[n1837]]. Bitcoin popped 6% on hints the reserve strategy was about to be revealed [[n1909]], which is the classic hook: the state is about to buy what the crowd already owns. The price says the trade is alive: bitcoin closed at 90,623.56 USD, up 7.41% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-05).
Where It Breaks

The reference close is 96,623.87, the bitcoin level from February 13 (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2025-03-05). Reclaiming it would mean the reserve premium is back. The downside marker is the $78K retest a bitcoin trader is eyeing while the US is seen delaying the reserve [[n1910]]. Instrument risk is flow: the crypto market saw a record $2.9 billion of outflows [[n1737]], and spot bitcoin ETFs once bled more than $1 billion in a single day [[n1548]]. Strategy is a levered proxy, and its 20-session decline of 11.42% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05) shows the leverage working in both directions.

retail.title: Leveraged ETFs / TQQQ and SOXL — three times the index, one day at a time
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Three-times funds are where small accounts express conviction after a drawdown. Bloomberg described Korean buyers who put money into leveraged ETFs and lost on Tesla [[n5753]], which is the same mechanism in another name. Yahoo Finance ranked the best-performing leveraged ETFs of February [[n5871]], and ETF Trends published the top performers for March 2 [[n6124]]. Options are part of the same urge: Bloomberg reported zero-day options trading hit a record on Trump-driven turmoil and a Robinhood push [[n5953]]. The crowd’s story is that the index always recovers, so a three-times fund is just a faster way to make the same bet. SOXL closed at 21.95 USD, up 6.30% in the prior session and down 16.51% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Where It Breaks

The trigger is a volatility spike. The VIX closed at 21.93 and is up 27.43% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05), and a three-times fund resets daily, so a choppy tape costs more than the index does. SOXL’s 20-session reference is 26.25 USD, and TQQQ’s is 83.65 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05). A close back above those references would mark a real leveraged bounce, and a break of the five-session lows would confirm the reset is still under way. Instrument risk is path dependence: TQQQ closed at 72.01 USD, down 13.92% over 20 sessions, and the daily reset means losses compound even if the index recovers.

retail.title: AST SpaceMobile / ASTS — the Starlink rival for phones
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Space is retail’s favourite speculative theme, and AST SpaceMobile is the one that fits in a sentence: a satellite network that works with ordinary phones. Vodafone agreed to build a European direct-to-device satellite service with it [[n5941]], and PCMag wrote that the Starlink rival is eyeing a major expansion in Europe [[n5926]]. A trading-education site, timothysykes.com, wrote up its game-changing moves [[n6060]], and SpaceNews framed the company as a path to European space sovereignty [[n6059]]. The price has done the rest: AST SpaceMobile closed at 33.80 USD, up 18.14% in the prior session, 24.08% over five sessions and 46.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05).
Where It Breaks

The trigger is the 20-session reference of 23.09 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2025-03-05): a close back below it would reverse the whole 20-session gain. The pending event is the European rollout with Vodafone, which is still a deal rather than revenue [[n5942]]. Instrument risk is size. A single-name space stock can move 18% in a session, and the company’s $43 million US government contract is a small item next to that [[n5766]].
